paperTitle: LABORAL: A Transformational Game for LER/DORT Prevention through Gesture-Interactions
centralContribution: This work introduces LABORAL, a transformational game designed for hand stretching using gesture-interactions, aiming to prevent and educate users about occupational diseases such as LER (Lesão por Esforço Repetitivo) / RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) and DORT (Distúrbio Osteomuscular Relacionado ao Trabalho) / WMSD (Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder), particularly for individuals who perform repetitive computer movements. The game fosters engaging learning and behavioral transformation regarding upper limb health.

units.title: LABORAL: Central Contribution
units.summary: Transformational game for LER/DORT prevention using gesture-interactions.

content.description: LABORAL is introduced as a transformational game for hand stretching, utilizing gesture-interactions to prevent and educate users about occupational diseases like LER/DORT. Its primary innovation lies in fostering engaging learning and behavioral transformation concerning upper limb health, particularly for individuals performing repetitive computer movements, by precisely implementing physiotherapist-defined stretching exercises.

units.title: Paper Abstract
units.summary: Overview of LER/DORT prevention via a 3D gesture-based game, LABORAL.

content.description: The increasing informatization of workplaces leads to prolonged occupational computer use, causing pain and severe occupational diseases like LER/DORT, which primarily affect upper limbs. While occupational gymnastics are preventive, their implementation is often lacking. Gesture recognition technologies, like the Leap Motion sensor, offer engaging alternatives for motor rehabilitation. This paper introduces LABORAL, a 3D transformational game developed with Unity and Leap Motion, focusing on precise, physiotherapist-defined stretching exercises to prevent LER/DORT, extending previous research by targeting specific therapeutic movements.

units.title: LABORAL System Architecture
units.summary: Overall architecture of the LABORAL game with Unity and Leap Motion.

content.description: A conceptual representation of the LABORAL game's architecture, illustrating its development with the Unity engine, the integration of the Leap Motion sensor for real-time gestural interaction, and the user interface design featuring pose cards, recognition indicators, exercise names, and a countdown timer. It demonstrates how these components collaborate to facilitate interactive hand stretching exercises.

units.conceptualOrigin: Defined Physiotherapy Stretching Sequences, Sequential Exercise Test Results: Execution Time and Failures

content.description: Outlines five fundamental hand stretching sequences, defined by a physiotherapist. Designed to target occupational conditions like tendinitis, carpal tunnel syndrome, and epicondylitis, detailing sequence names, number of poses, and target conditions.
content.title: Defined Physiotherapy Stretching Sequences

content.description: Presents average continuous execution times, frequent pose failure types, and overhead time versus discrete pose recognition for five exercise sequences. Highlights practical challenges in continuous gesture recognition for game efficacy.
